# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Rosalind Penrose is a tiny woman with an almost youthful face, rosy cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and large, gentle wood-brown eyes filled with tiny flecks of gold. She has lovely, thick, wavy snow-white hair thoughtfully set in flattering puffs and coils. Her voice is described as recalling white satin, splashing water, and fairy bells, and she wears a delicate cream muslin dress adorned with light-colored roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Rosalind is imaginative, gentle, and deeply hospitable, possessing a profound fondness for the company of young girls. Because she lives in an isolated location and sometimes feels lonely, she copes by pretending to hold tea parties with imaginary guests. Though considered peculiar by some locals for her unconventional habits and non-aging charm, she harbors deep sentimental feelings about her past.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P32](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0032), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)_

## Traits

- Imaginative  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>
- Hospitable  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058)</sub>
- Fond of young girls  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>
- Prone to feeling lonely  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P88](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0088)</sub>

## Abilities

- Pretending and imaginative play  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>

## Goals

- To entertain visitors and share company with young people  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c21 P78](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0078)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Penrose, who built an ancient sandstone house bounded by an overgrown dyke and spruces. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but their betrothal broke off following a disagreement twenty-five years prior, leading him to move to the States. Over time, she withdrew from social life and lived quietly in her stone dwelling with her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke lost their way in the woods, Rosalind invited them in to share tea that she had originally prepared for an imagined gathering. During their visit, Nell mentioned Cedric Stanhope, prompting Rosalind to inquire quietly if he was Stephen's son before parting with gifts of lavender. She later hosted Nell and Cedric for another tea at her stone home.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083), [v2 c21 P84](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0084), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036)_

## Background by volume

- Named Rosalind by her father because he loved the smell of lavender associated with meeting her mother  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Was formerly betrothed to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago before a disagreement ended their relationship  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am aware you will consider me terribly silly. I am silly . . . and I feel humiliated about it whenever I am caught, but only when I am caught. I am not awaiting anyone . . . I was merely imagining that I was.  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053)</sub>

> Occasionally, I doubt I could survive without imagining things.  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> At present, I need you to give me your names. It makes me very happy that you are young girls. Young girls are dear to me. Pretending to be a girl myself comes so naturally when I am in their company.  <sub>[v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062)</sub>

> Does Stephen Stanhope claim him as a son?  <sub>[v2 c21 P84](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0084)</sub>

> Each of you girls will get a cluster of lavender from me. Don’t you find it remarkably sweet?  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
